acceptance_criterion: Creating an unscheduled task does not create a calendar event.
Creating an arena reservation does not create a completion task unless a rule explicitly requires one.
A direct assignment is immediately active only when the assigning actor has authority.
An acceptance-required assignment remains pending until accepted or otherwise resolved.
A claimable task can be claimed only by an actor in the authorized pool.
Completion records preserve actor, actual time, entry time, instruction version, evidence status, and sync status.
Backdated completion preserves the original escalation history.
Editing one recurrence occurrence does not alter completed history or unrelated future occurrences.
Editing this-and-following splits or versions the series deterministically.
An imported external event is visibly labeled and does not silently create an operational task.
External event deletion follows the approved conflict policy and does not silently destroy EquineSync truth.
A hard resource conflict blocks save absent an authorized override.
A soft conflict requires a visible warning and confirmation.
Unknown availability is displayed as unknown.
Authoritative time remains stable when a user travels across time zones.
DST ambiguity is handled deterministically and visibly.
Viewing or acknowledging a notification does not complete its task.
Quiet hours suppress routine notices but not an authorized safety-critical override.
An urgent notice does not disappear inside a routine digest.
A failed email can fall back to another approved channel according to policy.
Optional SMS is sent only to a verified, permitted destination under applicable consent and opt-out rules.
SMS failure enters retry or failed-delivery administration without being treated as refusal.
Duplicate provider webhooks do not duplicate notification state transitions.
A missed welfare-sensitive task escalates according to its risk policy.
Completing, canceling, or reassigning a task changes escalation behavior according to the state model.
Delegation does not expose unrelated horse, owner, medical, billing, or facility records.
A generated task identifies its source record and rule version.
Changing the source schedule produces the defined update, cancellation, or review behavior.
AI cannot silently assign a high-risk task.
A personal reminder may be disabled without deleting an authoritative operational requirement.
A mandatory reminder cannot be disabled through ordinary user preferences.
Offline completion remains visibly pending until synchronization.
Repeated sync does not duplicate completion, evidence, or notification.
Conflicting offline completions enter reconciliation rather than silently overwriting one another.
Revoked access prevents new offline retrieval and is reconciled on reconnect.
Administrators can inspect failed delivery, retry history, recipient resolution, and channel evidence without reading unrelated content.
Support correction preserves the original record and reason.
Feature-flag disablement stops new external sync while preserving recoverable state and evidence.
The first-release capability set excludes advanced workforce and AI scheduling optimization.
The readiness section uses only permitted answer values and does not claim implementation or enrollment authority.
A task dependency cycle is rejected without altering existing valid dependencies.
Bulk task action applies only to items for which the actor passes per-record authorization and returns item-level results.
RSVP acceptance does not create assignment, payment, consent, or professional authority.
An availability request may return busy without revealing a restricted title, horse, minor, location, or participant.
A material schedule change sends versioned updates to the policy-defined affected recipients and resources.
A notification record preserves the exact template version, locale, channel rendering, and redaction policy used.
An optional SMS opt-out stops future optional SMS while preserving required in-app or other lawful mandatory communication.
SMS volume or spend exceeding the configured limit blocks or pauses additional optional sends and alerts an authorized operator.
A provider outage is displayed as provider degradation and does not mark native tasks or notices successful.
A P0 or P1 operational condition generates the defined alert and incident record within its target.
Backup restore reproduces linked task, event, occurrence, completion, notification, escalation, and audit relationships without orphaning.
Provider exit revokes credentials and disables new sends or sync while preserving native records and evidence.
A migration dry run produces no authoritative mutation and yields deterministic reconciliation reports.
Synthetic seed data is visibly labeled, isolated, and cannot be mistaken for a real horse, person, task, or notification.
The first-user gate yields a reproducible ready or not-ready determination without implying authorization before Founder disposition.
